evidence.detail: rs/d/s owns a static Map<String,rs/d/s$a> whose dynamic object packet keys are built exactly as x,y,plane, so one override is tracked per world tile/plane coordinate.

The object-update packet removes a coordinate key and calls Client.a(x,y,-1,0,10,plane) to clear an object; its add path creates an rs/d/s$a record, stores it by coordinate and calls Client.a(x,y,objectId,rotation,type,plane).
The packet's third action scans the registry for records with a requested object id, clears each matching object from the scene through the same Client.a spawn API and removes those registry entries.
rs/d/s.a(Client) contains the client's large built-in table of fixed world-coordinate object additions, replacements and removals, all applied through the same six-argument object-spawn API.

candidates.note: ObjectSpawnOverrideManager is the conservative semantic name for this exact built-in/dynamic object-spawn override registry and applicator; it does not claim a verbatim original developer identifier.

evidence.detail: rs/d/s$a is a six-int data record populated directly from the object-update packet before being placed in the manager's coordinate-keyed override map.
The manager replays the record as Client.a(x,y,objectId,rotation,type,plane), while removal reuses its x/y/plane coordinates with object id -1.
The record is stored only inside ObjectSpawnOverrideManager's x,y,plane registry and is iterated there for object-id based bulk removal.

candidates.note: ObjectSpawnOverride is the conservative semantic name for this exact object-id/coordinate/type/rotation/plane override record; it does not claim a verbatim original developer identifier.
